note: Tables the worker queries that nothing creates, each reviewed and each a feature whose store was never built rather than a typo. Every one is a guarded read that degrades to empty — none can throw. The gate fails on NEW entries, and also on entries here that have since been created, so this list cannot go stale. Fixing one means deleting its line.

tables.advisor_sessions: the Telegram and X weekly aggregators (services/telegramAggregator.ts, services/xAggregator.ts). Read through safeCount, which returns 0 on error, so the digest reports 'advisor sessions: 0' every week whatever happened. Invisible until D184 widened the harvest: safeCount takes the SQL as an argument, so no anchored extractor ever saw it. advisor_slots is a different (also absent) table; the sessions that DO exist are expert_bookings.
tables.advisor_slots: the advisor onboarding checklist's mt.slots item (services/onboardingChecklist.ts). Read through num(), which returns 0 on error, so the item reads 'not done' for every advisor, forever. sql/historical/schema.sql:961 is the ONLY CREATE TABLE for it in the repo and its column there is mentor_user_id, not user_id — so this was never satisfiable even before the table was archived. D184 is what made it visible: the tables guard had been harvesting sql/historical/ and calling it known.
tables.compliance_tasks: advisor tool `listMyTasks` (services/advisor/tools.ts). Query is wrapped and degrades to an empty list, so the advisor answers 'no tasks' to everyone. No compliance-task store has ever been built; workflow_tasks is a different thing (studio operations, not per-user compliance).
tables.introductions: the Telegram and X weekly aggregators. safeCount degrades to 0, so the digest's introductions line is always zero. investor_introductions exists and is the real store — this is a name that was never created, not a rename of it, since the aggregators want a platform-wide count and investor_introductions would give one.
tables.kyc_records: the investor checklist's inv.kyc item and the partner checklist's op.kyb item (services/onboardingChecklist.ts). num() degrades to 0, so both read 'not done' for everyone, forever. No KYC/KYB record store exists anywhere in the repo — corporate_profiles.kyb_status in the columns baseline is the other half of the same absence, and D108 already recorded that the KYB decision path has no writer.
tables.linkedin_oauth_tokens: settings integration summary (routes/settings.ts, two sites). Both reads go through safeOne, which returns false on error, so LinkedIn always renders as disconnected. google_oauth_tokens and microsoft_oauth_tokens exist (sql/calendar.sql); the LinkedIn OAuth flow that would write this one was never built — routes/linkedin.ts stores only a profile picture URL.
tables.matches: the Telegram weekly aggregator. safeCount degrades to 0. match_scores exists and holds the scores; `matches` as a table name has never existed.
tables.partner_office_hours: the Telegram and X weekly aggregators. safeCount degrades to 0, so the office-hours line is always zero. The partners table carries oh_* columns (oh_when_to_book, oh_stage_fit, …) which are guidance copy, not booked sessions — there is no session store behind them.
tables.refer_earn_payouts: the Telegram weekly aggregator. safeCount degrades to 0. The refer-and-earn feature exists (referral_invites, referral_submissions) but no payout ledger was ever built for it.
tables.spinout_lab_state: the trust-score graduate signal (services/newsTrust.ts:78). safeFirst degrades to null, so spinout_grad is never awarded its 10 points. The Spin-Out Lab's own state lives in cohort_applicants and company_week_status; no table of this name exists.
tables.subscription_events: billing history in services/analyticsReports.ts. Deliberately optional: the query is followed by a documented fallback that synthesizes one row from the current users.mi_subscription_* state, so the admin report is correct-but-shallow rather than wrong.
